title: Non-Zero Digits Times Their Sum
statement:
You get a non-negative integer n. Drop every 0 digit from it and read the digits that are left, in their original order, as a new number x. If no digits are left, x = 0.

Return x multiplied by the sum of the digits of x.

examples.why: Without zeros the digits read 432. Their sum is 9, and 432 × 9 = 3888. Multiplying the original 40302 by 9 would be wrong.
Nothing is left after dropping the zero, so x = 0 and the product is 0.

hints: Work digit by digit. Which digits survive, and in what order?
You need two things from the surviving digits: the number they spell and their sum. One pass can build both.
Peeling digits with % 10 gives them right to left. Keep a place value that grows by 10 only when you keep a digit, so the zeros leave no gap.

explain.intuition:
This is a warm-up in handling digits. The only subtle part is that removing a zero closes the gap: 40302 becomes 432, not 40302 with zeros ignored in the sum only.

The easy route is a string: filter out '0' characters and parse. The arithmetic route peels digits with % 10 from the right. Each kept digit goes at the current place value, and the place value moves up by a factor of 10 only for kept digits. That is the same as squeezing the zeros out.
steps: While n > 0: take d = n % 10 and set n = floor(n / 10).
If d ≠ 0: add d × place to x, add d to sum, multiply place by 10.
pitfalls: Multiplying the original n by the digit sum. The zeros must be removed from the number itself.
Moving the place value up for zeros too. That keeps the gaps and rebuilds n.
Using 32-bit arithmetic. 999999999 gives about 8·1010, which needs a 64-bit integer in typed languages.

solutions.title: Filter the digit string
solutions.idea: Turn n into a string, keep the non-zero characters, parse what is left and add up its digits.

solutions.title: Peel digits with a place value
solutions.idea: Read digits right to left. A kept digit lands at the current place value, and only kept digits move the place value up.

followups: n arrives as a string of up to 10<sup>5</sup> digits and you must return the answer modulo 10<sup>9</sup> + 7. How do you build x without big integers?
Answer the same question for many substrings of one long digit string. What would you precompute?
